---
title: "Module 01: Assemble single-cell RNA-seq Seurat object"
output: html_document
---

```{r}

#==============================================================================
# MODULE 01 — Assemble single-cell RNA-seq Seurat object
#==============================================================================

# Purpose:
#   Import raw 10x count matrices, create sample-level Seurat objects,
#   harmonize genes across samples, merge samples, calculate basic QC metadata,
#   and save objects for downstream analysis.
#
# Input:
#   data/raw/single_cell_raw/
#
# Output:
#   data/processed/single_cell/
#
# Notes:
#   Only permissive filtering is applied during object creation
#   (min.cells = 3, min.features = 200).
#   Detailed cell-level QC is performed in Module 02.


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Setup
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(Matrix)
  library(here)
})

set.seed(1234)

input_directory <- here::here(
  "data",
  "raw",
  "single_cell_raw"
)

processed_directory <- here::here(
  "data",
  "processed",
  "single_cell"
)

dir.create(
  processed_directory,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

if (!dir.exists(input_directory)) {
  stop(
    "Input directory not found: ",
    input_directory
  )
}


# Define samples used in the analysis.
# Add or remove rows here when adapting the workflow to another dataset.

sample_info <- data.frame(
  sample = c(
    "C2_S2",
    "N1_S3",
    "N2_S4"
  ),
  gsm = c(
    "GSM9021009",
    "GSM9021010",
    "GSM9021011"
  ),
  condition = c(
    "Control",
    "Niacin",
    "Niacin"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

print(sample_info)


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create sample-level Seurat objects
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

create_seurat_object <- function(
  gsm,
  sample_name,
  condition,
  input_directory
) {

  message("Loading ", sample_name, "...")

  matrix_file <- file.path(
    input_directory,
    paste0(gsm, "_", sample_name, "_matrix.mtx.gz")
  )

  barcode_file <- file.path(
    input_directory,
    paste0(gsm, "_", sample_name, "_barcodes.tsv.gz")
  )

  feature_file <- file.path(
    input_directory,
    paste0(gsm, "_", sample_name, "_features.tsv.gz")
  )

  required_files <- c(
    matrix_file,
    barcode_file,
    feature_file
  )

  missing_files <- required_files[
    !file.exists(required_files)
  ]

  if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Missing input file(s) for ",
      sample_name,
      ":\n",
      paste(missing_files, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }


  counts <- ReadMtx(
    mtx = matrix_file,
    cells = barcode_file,
    features = feature_file,
    feature.column = 2
  )


  # Apply only permissive filtering during object creation.
  # Detailed QC filtering is performed in Module 02.

  seurat_object <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts,
    project = sample_name,
    min.cells = 3,
    min.features = 200
  )


  # Add sample-level metadata.

  seurat_object$sample <- sample_name
  seurat_object$condition <- condition
  seurat_object$GSM <- gsm


  message(
    sample_name,
    ": ",
    nrow(seurat_object),
    " genes x ",
    ncol(seurat_object),
    " cells"
  )

  return(seurat_object)
}


# Process all samples defined in sample_info.

single_cell_objects <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(sample_info)),
  function(i) {

    create_seurat_object(
      gsm = sample_info$gsm[i],
      sample_name = sample_info$sample[i],
      condition = sample_info$condition[i],
      input_directory = input_directory
    )
  }
)

names(single_cell_objects) <- sample_info$sample


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Harmonize genes across samples
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Retain a common feature space across all samples before merging.

common_genes <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  lapply(
    single_cell_objects,
    rownames
  )
)

if (length(common_genes) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No genes are shared across all samples."
  )
}

single_cell_objects <- lapply(
  single_cell_objects,
  subset,
  features = common_genes
)

message(
  "Shared genes retained: ",
  length(common_genes)
)


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Merge samples
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

message("Merging samples...")

single_cell_merged <- merge(
  x = single_cell_objects[[1]],
  y = single_cell_objects[-1],
  add.cell.ids = names(single_cell_objects),
  project = "GSE298688"
)

DefaultAssay(single_cell_merged) <- "RNA"

message(
  "Merged object: ",
  nrow(single_cell_merged),
  " genes x ",
  ncol(single_cell_merged),
  " cells"
)


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Calculate basic QC metadata
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate mitochondrial transcript percentage.
# This dataset uses mouse-style mitochondrial gene names beginning with "mt-".

mitochondrial_genes <- grep(
  "^mt-",
  rownames(single_cell_merged),
  value = TRUE
)

if (length(mitochondrial_genes) == 0) {

  warning(
    "No mitochondrial genes matched '^mt-'. ",
    "Confirm the gene naming convention."
  )

} else {

  single_cell_merged[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(
    single_cell_merged,
    pattern = "^mt-"
  )
}


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Inspect assembled object
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

required_metadata <- c(
  "sample",
  "condition",
  "GSM",
  "nCount_RNA",
  "nFeature_RNA",
  "percent.mt"
)

missing_metadata <- setdiff(
  required_metadata,
  colnames(single_cell_merged@meta.data)
)

if (length(missing_metadata) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing required metadata: ",
    paste(
      missing_metadata,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}


# Review basic QC metrics before detailed filtering in Module 02.

summary(
  single_cell_merged@meta.data[
    ,
    c(
      "nCount_RNA",
      "nFeature_RNA",
      "percent.mt"
    )
  ]
)

cat("\nCells per sample:\n")

print(
  table(
    single_cell_merged$sample
  )
)

cat("\nCells per condition:\n")

print(
  table(
    single_cell_merged$condition
  )
)


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save objects
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Save individual sample objects.

for (sample_name in names(single_cell_objects)) {

  output_file <- file.path(
    processed_directory,
    paste0(
      sample_name,
      "_raw_seurat.rds"
    )
  )

  saveRDS(
    single_cell_objects[[sample_name]],
    output_file
  )

  message(
    "Saved: ",
    output_file
  )
}


# Save merged object.

merged_output_file <- file.path(
  processed_directory,
  "GSE298688_merged_raw_seurat.rds"
)

saveRDS(
  single_cell_merged,
  merged_output_file
)

message(
  "Saved merged object: ",
  merged_output_file
)

message("Module 01 complete.")

```
